source_evidence: Investors in hedge funds typically pay an asset management fee of 1-2% of NAV. In addition, they also typically pay a performance fee of 15-20% of the hedge fund’s profit subject to certain measures, such as a high-water mark and a hurdle rate, which can limit when a manager is entitled to performance fees.
answer: Hedge funds typically charge two kinds of fees. An asset management fee is generally 1–2% of the fund’s net asset value (NAV). A performance fee is generally 15–20% of the fund’s profit, but conditions such as a high-water mark or hurdle rate can limit when the manager earns it. Fees reduce investors’ returns over time, and a performance fee may encourage a manager to take greater risks in pursuit of a larger return.
